content_voiceover: This is the INO-VATE trial, a phase three randomized study of inotuzumab ozogamicin, an anti-CD22 antibody drug conjugate, in relapsed or refractory CD22 positive B cell ALL. Three hundred twenty six adults on first or second salvage were randomized to inotuzumab, dosed weekly over a twenty one to twenty eight day cycle for up to six cycles, versus standard of care chemotherapy such as FLAG, cytarabine plus mitoxantrone, or high dose Ara-C. The two co-primary endpoints were complete remission, including CR with incomplete count recovery, and overall survival. The results were striking. The complete remission or CR with incomplete hematologic recovery rate was eighty one percent with inotuzumab versus only twenty nine percent with standard therapy, a highly significant difference. Complete remission alone was also markedly higher, about thirty six percent versus seventeen percent. Bone marrow blast clearance below the threshold for minimal residual disease was likewise much better with inotuzumab. This established inotuzumab as a highly active salvage option in CD22 positive relapsed refractory ALL.
keypoints: INO-VATE phase three trial, anti-CD22 ADC inotuzumab ozogamicin versus standard chemo in R R B-ALL
Three hundred twenty six adults, randomized one to one, up to six cycles of inotuzumab
CR plus CRi rate eighty one percent with inotuzumab versus twenty nine percent with standard of care
Bone marrow MRD negativity rate substantially higher with inotuzumab
keypoint_voiceover: Remember INO-VATE as the pivotal trial for inotuzumab ozogamicin in CD22 positive relapsed refractory B cell ALL. It randomized over three hundred adults to inotuzumab versus standard chemotherapy, and inotuzumab achieved an eighty one percent complete remission or CRi rate compared with twenty nine percent for standard of care, along with much deeper MRD negativity.
